newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Telefonica international tranche could fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Telefonica international tranche could fall.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica on Friday said it could not guarantee to international investors that their allocation in its forthcoming share sale would not be cut because of the need to satisfy strong domestic demand.

The majority-privatised telecommunications group, launching a roadshow to attract international investors, also appeared to cast doubt over the start-date of its digital television consortium, suggesting it had encountered delays.
Chairman Juan Villalonga told a news briefing after a presentation to Frankfurt-based investors that he could not currently rule out a situation under which the international tranche was reduced.
Under initial allocation plans for the public offering of 171.1 million shares, the international tranche is slated to represent 42 percent of the issue.
However, the offering can be increased to 196.7 million shares to allow the domestic tranche to be expanded to 68 percent, with the international allocation dropping to 32 percent.

"It can go further (below the 32 percent level)," Villalonga said, adding that the domestic retail side of the offering, due for final pricing on February 17, was already some seven times oversubscribed.

"We want to satisfy the demands of all the Spaniards who want to be shareholders," he said. He added that the fact that the offering could be expanded meant however there was a certain flexibility in responding to demand.

Local Spanish media have speculated that the domestic allocation could rise to as much as 75 percent. Villalonga said he did have a minimum level in mind for the international tranche to go but did not specify what that was.

Frankfurt was the first stop on an international roadshow ahead of the sale of the Spanish state's remaining 20.9 percent stake in Telefonica. Further presentations around Europe, the United States and the Far East are planned.

Telefonica also appeared to retreat from a recent forecast that the digital television platform it is backing in Spain could be up and running in March, saying there had been delays linked to its partners in the project.
"It will now come some time later, before the summer," Juan Perea, director of strategic planning and control, told the news briefing.
Perea said there had been delays relating to the other partners in the project and their involvement with the platform, without giving further details.

Telefonica said this week its digital TV project had been legally formed under the name of Digital Television Distributor (DTD), with other partners drawn from the broadcasting and wider media sector.

Earlier on Friday, Spain's government cabinet said it had approved new legislation that will mean that any television decoder brought onto the market will have to be compatible with those from other suppliers.
Spain's first digital platform was launched on Thursday by Canal Satellite. The decoders ordered for the service will not meet the new requirements specified by the regulation.
